TECHNIQUE / OPEN FOLLOW-UP -- plan-hygiene's DELETION OF IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md WAS UNDONE ON main WITHIN THE HOUR, BY THE EXACT MECHANISM THAT MOTIVATED IT. The session that landed it has ended; this is for whoever picks the work up.

    $ git show origin/main:IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md | head -1
    # Eclipse Rhythm and View

main c0b76af87 carries that file TRACKED, while main's own .gitignore lists it,
and its content is campaign/eclipse-rhythm-view's plan.

HOW. campaign/plan-hygiene deleted and gitignored it at 0d266b32a.
campaign/the-planetarium had earlier absorbed main while eclipse's copy was
present, so their branch carried it as INHERITED content. Their merge ran after
plan-hygiene landed; the modify/delete resolved toward keeping the file. Nobody
decided that, nothing warned, and the file simply reappeared.

That is plan-hygiene's own headline finding reproducing itself: 14 of ~20
branches carried a copy they had inherited by absorb and had no relationship
to. The change landed to end that, and was reverted by an instance of it inside
an hour.

THE DURABILITY GAP, which is the part worth acting on. A .gitignore entry does
NOT evict a tracked file. It stops the file being ADDED afresh; it has no
opinion about one arriving through a merge. So the deletion is only as durable
as every subsequent conflict resolution on every branch still carrying it — and
several still do.

NOTHING DETECTS A RESURRECTION TODAY:
  - no test asserts the path is untracked
  - `git diff --exit-code` over docs/generated-paths.txt has no opinion on a
    path nobody declared (and CLAUDE.md already warns that check is silently
    vacuous against undeclared paths)
  - the mouth classifies the conflict as ordinary, because it is

THE SHAPE OF A FIX, in an idiom this repo already runs: an assertion that the
path is untracked, the way `cli/tests/suite/test_binary_ratchet.rs` freezes the
top-level tests/*.rs roster and `temp_path_ratchet` freezes fixed temp paths.
Cheap, default-deny, and it converts "deleted once" into "stays deleted". The
author of plan-hygiene proposed exactly that idiom for a different guard and
then correctly abandoned it on evidence; this one has a demonstrated instance
rather than a hypothesis — the deletion has already been reverted once.

IMMEDIATE STATE: campaign/the-planetarium's follow-up candidate (489e00f3663b)
modifies the file again and is HELD. I have asked them to `git rm` it, which
both restores the deletion and makes their candidate prose-only — that file is
the sole disqualifier, worth ~11 minutes of clients+heavy. Verified by running
sluice_is_prose_only over their real changed set both ways.
